card.caption: Every incumbent stops at “recommend → you click.” Reorder Loop is the missing last mile — built carefully, proven in shadow first.

identify.title: Every order is a bet — and you’re the only one allowed to place it.

one.body: 40 units left of the thing everybody does.

two.body: The last invoice still doesn’t match what landed, and you paid it anyway.

three.statement: The spreadsheet says lead time, MOQ, last order date.
three.body: It doesn’t say what it costs you when you’re wrong.

four.statement: Nobody else in the company can make this call.
four.body: It’s your cash. So it’s your night.

identify.closer: You didn’t start a brand to run purchasing after dinner.

logic.title: The whole order, done — not another number to act on

one.title: Sized to your cash
one.body: Every order gets sized to what’s actually selling, and to the cash you actually have. Not too much. Not too little. Not too late.

two.title: You hear it the day it happens
two.body: When the supplier says “we can only do 800, three weeks late,” you know the day they say it — not the day the shelf is empty.

three.title: You pay for what landed
three.body: When 1,180 units land and you were billed for 1,200, you don’t pay for the 20.

logic.footer: And for the first 30 days it touches nothing. It shows you every order it would have placed, next to the one you did. You compare. Then you decide.

objections.title: The three reasons not to believe this — answered

one.q: “I’m not letting software spend my money.”
one.a: Good. It doesn’t. For 30 days it spends nothing. After that, nothing goes out without your yes. After that, only inside limits you set. You stay in charge — always.

two.q: “I could build this with Claude in a weekend.”
two.a: The forecast, sure. The weekend script doesn’t read the supplier’s reply. Doesn’t catch the short-ship. Doesn’t notice when it quietly stops working. And nobody’s watching when it does.

three.a: It tells you what to order. Then you email the supplier, chase the container, and check the invoice. The forecast was never the hard part.

confess.title: We had the same fear.
confess.sub: It’s why nine apps forecast and none finish the order — nobody wanted to be the one committing your cash. So we built it to earn that, on your own orders, before it touches a thing.

solution.title: Your cash, untrapped.
solution.sub: Cash where it sells. Bestsellers on the shelf. Evenings back.
solution.withoutBody: Every order is still yours. Still at night. Still a bet. One bad one and the cash is gone — buried in the wrong boxes, or missing from the shelf when it mattered.
solution.withBody: You open one message. Here’s the order. Here’s why. You say yes. The rest happens without you.
